name: Question 1
problem:
Suppose $n=-2p+6q-10,$ where $p,q\in Z.$ Complete the following argument.

The number $n$ is {{field-1}} since 

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =-2p+6q-10 \\  & =2({{field-2}}-5) \\  & ={{field-3}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $a=${{field-4}}.
worked_solution:
An integer is *even* if it can be written as $2a,$ where $a$ is an integer.

Notice that all terms in the expression $-2p+6q-10$ have a common factor of $2.$ 

Therefore, we complete our argument as follows:

The number $n$ is $\text{even}$ since

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =-2p+6q-10 \\  & =2({{-p+3q-5}_{⏟}}_{a}) \\  & =2a,\end{aligned}
$$

where $a=-p+3q-5\in Z.$
